sections.h2: Which Genesee County office keeps recorded deeds?
sections.html:
The County Clerk and Register of Deeds does, from the Genesee County Administration Building at 324 S Saginaw St, Suite 1A, Flint, MI 48502. Hours on the county page run weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00, with holiday closings.

One elected office oversees vital records, elections and the register of deeds. The register's collection covers deeds, mortgages, liens and other papers touching Genesee land. The county page puts it bluntly: filing makes a paper public and does not make it legal. Staff index each filing into a searchable database and preserve it, so a flawed deed stays flawed after it is on file.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees in Genesee County?
sections.html:
The statewide default is a flat $30 per recorded document, whatever its length. Charter counties can pass their own schedule, so get the current sheet from the office before you mail payment.

Service (MCL 600.2567)Charge
Record one document$30
Extra instruments covered by one discharge or assignment$3 apiece
Photocopies$1 per page
Certification of a recorded paper$5
Index search by request$0.50 per year, $5 floor
Other filings$1

Reference: MCL 600.2567. The $30 already includes the state remonumentation share, and $5 of each recording goes to the register's automation fund.

Fees are due at drop-off. If the register takes electronic filings and you pay electronically, the statute gives one business day after receipt. Ask whether Genesee takes e-filing before you plan a closing around it.

sections.h2: Which taxes does the deed trigger when it is recorded in Genesee County?
sections.html:
A sale deed brings two levies, and the seller owes both. Michigan's rate is $3.75 per $500 of price, rounded up by $500 block, and the county adds 55 cents on each block because its population is under two million.

The deed must carry the total value in its text, or a value affidavit goes with it. When land and personal property sell together with separate stated values, only the land is taxed. Remit to the county treasurer within 15 days of handing over the deed. At $120,000 there are 240 blocks, so $900 goes to the state and $132 to the county.

  • Tiny deals: instruments under $100.
  • Loan paper: mortgages and other collateral documents, with their assignments and discharges.
  • Gifts to descendants: deeds from a parent to a child or grandchild avoid the state levy.
  • Lender foreclosure: transfers made through foreclosure or in place of it, though a resale afterward is taxed.
  • Land contracts: exempt until legal title passes.

A seller who overpaid on an exempt transfer may request a refund from the Department of Treasury.

sections.h2: Which papers does a Genesee County house sale put on record?
sections.html:
A typical sale records a deed and, where a mortgage existed, a discharge. Each is filed separately with its own fee.

  • Deed: warranty, quitclaim or personal representative form.
  • Mortgage discharge or assignment: $30, plus $3 for every extra instrument it covers.
  • Tax foreclosure papers: forfeiture and redemption certificates, notices of judgment and auction deeds. Their fees may be settled within 30 days after the sale or transfer.
  • Transfer affidavit: kept with the local assessor, which in Flint is the city Assessments Division, so it never reaches the register.

The county page does not list electronic options, so ask what the office accepts for each paper.

sections.h2: What does a tax foreclosure judgment do to recorded title?
sections.html:
It clears most of what is on the books. When the judgment takes effect on March 31, title vests in the foreclosing unit, which in Genesee is the county treasurer, and liens and interests on the parcel are extinguished. The state timeline names what survives: future installments of special assessments, environmental liens filed by government agencies, severed or leased oil and gas interests, visible or recorded easements and private deed restrictions.

The paper trail lands at the register's desk. A notice of judgment goes on record, and later so does the deed from an auction. Redemption stays open through March 31. After that date the former owner has no claim, and the buyer at the county auction relies on the recorded deed.

sections.h2: How far back do Genesee County's land descriptions go?
sections.html:
Genesee County's land history starts in the 1830s, which is why old deeds can describe parcels by township surveys that no longer match today's boundaries. The Legislature created the county on March 28, 1835 from land taken from Lapeer, Shiawassee and Saginaw counties, and for a time it was attached to Oakland County for court purposes. Grand Blanc, organized in 1833, was the only township at first.

Flint Township followed on March 2, 1836, and the county was fully organized that April 4. More townships were carved out over the next two decades, among them Genesee, Fenton, Flushing, Thetford, Gaines, Clayton and Mount Morris, and in 1843 a column of townships along the eastern edge, including Davison and Atlas, was added from Lapeer County. An old legal description may therefore cite a township that has since been split.

For a seller, the lesson is practical. If a deed in your chain uses an older description, or a township that was later renamed or split, tell the title company early so any correction deed can be recorded before the sale closes.

sections.h2: Where do the other Genesee County property records sit?
sections.html:
Four offices hold the records a seller is likely to need, and only the register holds the recorded documents.

  • Register of Deeds, Suite 1A: deeds, mortgages, discharges, liens and foreclosure notices.
  • Equalization, Suite 8B: parcel descriptions and land records for every municipality except Flint, with assessment data left to the local assessor.
  • Flint Assessments Division: Flint's own parcel records, transfer affidavits, splits and combinations.
  • County Treasurer, Suite 2A: payoffs on delinquent tax and foreclosure information.

Before closing, order a payoff from the treasurer if tax is overdue, and confirm with the assessor that the parcel description matches the deed.

sections.h2: Why does the Genesee County record matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Title companies and buyers read it as the public chain of ownership. A discharge nobody filed, or a misspelled grantor name, has to be corrected before a closing can finish.

The Census Bureau counts 185,007 housing units and 167,334 households in Genesee, with owners in 70.7% of homes and a midpoint owner-occupied value of $182,400, against $53,500 in Flint. Six counties ring it: Tuscola, Lapeer, Oakland, Livingston, Shiawassee and Saginaw. I-75, I-69 and I-475 cross its middle.

A seller with a house that needs work or carries back tax can sell as-is for cash, and the payoff comes out of the proceeds when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: What does the register charge to file a deed in Genesee County?
faqs.a: The state's baseline in MCL 600.2567 is $30 per document of any length. Because charter counties can set their own amounts, confirm the current Genesee County figure with the office before you pay.

faqs.q: Where do I find the Genesee County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is in the County Administration Building, 324 S Saginaw St, Suite 1A, Flint, MI 48502. The county page lists weekday hours of 8:00 to 4:00, excluding holidays.

faqs.q: Is a recorded deed automatically valid?
faqs.a: No. The county's own page says recording makes a document public and does not make it legal. The deed still needs proper signatures, a correct description and a grantor who owns the land.

faqs.q: Who writes the transfer tax check when a Genesee County house sells?
faqs.a: The seller does, to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed changes hands. The two levies are $3.75 and 55 cents on each $500 block of price.

faqs.q: Do I owe transfer tax on a deed to my child?
faqs.a: A deed to a child, stepchild, adopted child, grandchild or step-grandchild escapes the state tax. The deed is still recorded, and the usual filing fee applies.
